subject.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent

question: Which trusted representation of the requester’s resolved sender policy should a spawned subagent inherit without copying untrusted channel identity fields?
rationale: The patch currently chooses policy omission, while preserving exact sender restrictions requires an explicit security-boundary design for trusted inheritance across the spawn/session boundary.

options.title: Persist resolved policy snapshot
options.body: Store the parent’s resolved sender policy in the trusted subagent capability envelope and apply it to every child run before subagent restrictions.

options.title: Propagate verified identity metadata
options.body: Carry only server-verified sender identity metadata through the spawn boundary and re-resolve toolsBySender for the child.

options.title: Limit the bypass
options.body: Skip wildcard resolution only when the parent policy is demonstrably non-restrictive, leaving restrictive exact policies fail-closed until inheritance is implemented.

recommendation.title: Persist resolved policy snapshot
recommendation.body: Store the parent’s resolved sender policy in the trusted subagent capability envelope and apply it to every child run before subagent restrictions.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice affects the shared core agent capability and subagent security boundary, where recent adjacent core history provides the strongest available routing signal.
